title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)
body: Elliptic curves are cubic curves of the form \(y^2 = x^3 + ax + b\) that carry a natural abelian group structure.

The security of elliptic curve cryptography rests on the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem (ECDLP): given two points \(P\) and \(Q = kP\) on a curve, find the scalar \(k\). No sub-exponential algorithm is known for this in general, which means ECC achieves the same security as RSA with much smaller key sizes.
ECC underlies key exchange in TLS/HTTPS, SSH, Bitcoin, etc.
This project works with curves in short Weierstrass form over two types of fields: the rationals \(\mathbb{Q}\) and prime fields \(\mathbb{F}_p\) (characteristic \(\neq 2, 3\)).

body.html:
• A Python library for elliptic curve arithmetic (point addition, doubling, and scalar multiplication) implemented field-agnostically to work on \(\mathbb{Q}\) and \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
  • An algorithm to compute the group structure \(E(\mathbb{F}_p) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n_1\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/n_2\mathbb{Z}\) of an elliptic curve over a finite field and explicit generators \(e_1, e_2\) for each cyclic factor.
